_source.text: Before Mr. Sergeant Arabin. 1814. THOMAS CARTWRIGHT was indicted for stealing, on the 29th of June , 12 half-crowns, 40 shillings, and 20 sixpences, the monies of Thomas Cunnington , his master . THOMAS CUNNINGTON . I am a farmer , and live at Hampstead ; the prisoner was in my employ for about two months, and has been in and out of my place for twelve months. On the 29th of June when I went away from dinner, I left word for them to send me down 4l. of silver to pay the hay-makers; the prisoner
_source.title: THOMAS CARTWRIGHT. Theft; stealing from master. 6th September 1832.

text: three weeks afterwards at Hampstead. CAROLINE COLSTONE . I live with the prosecutor. I gave the prisoner about 4l., and desired him to take it to the field and give it to his master, on the 29th of June - it was Mr. Cunnington's money. EMANUEL TURNER (<mark>Police</mark>-constable S 15.) I took the prisoner. GUILTY . Aged 15. - Transported for Seven Years .

_source.text: 1815. JOSEPH DOLLY was indicted for stealing, on the 9th of July , 1 pair of stays, value 2s., and 1 shirt, value 1s. 4d. , the goods of John Boards . CHARLES RANDYLL (Police-constable H 68). On the 9th of July I was at the corner of Phoenix-street, Bricklane, and saw the prisoner carrying a bundle; I asked what he had there - he said a pair of stays of his wife's; I took him. _source.text: 1816. JOHN JONES was indicted for stealing, on the 7th of July , 1 handkerchief, value 3s., the goods of Samuel Adolphus Philbrick , from his person . SAMUEL ADOLPHUS PHILBRICK . I am a surgeon . On the 7th of July, between one and two o'clock in the day, I was in Whitechapel ; I had a handkerchief in my pocket; I felt something, and turned round; I saw the prisoner with my handkerchief in his hand; I collared him, and asked him for it - he gave it me. ROBERT ADAMS . I am a City Police constable
_source.title: JOHN JONES. Theft; pocketpicking. 6th September 1832.

text: 1816. JOHN JONES was indicted for stealing, on the 7th of July , 1 handkerchief, value 3s., the goods of Samuel Adolphus Philbrick , from his person . SAMUEL ADOLPHUS PHILBRICK . I am a <mark>surgeon</mark> . On the 7th of July, between one and two o'clock in the day, I was in Whitechapel ; I had a handkerchief

in my pocket; I felt something, and turned round; I saw the prisoner with my handkerchief in his hand; I collared him, and asked him for it - he gave it me. ROBERT ADAMS . I am a City <mark>Police</mark> constable, No. 19. I took the prisoner, and have the handkerchief. The prisoner put in a written Defence, stating that he had found the handkerchief under a fruit stall. GUILTY . Aged 19. - Transported for Fourteen Years .

_source.text: 1817. JAMES JEFFERIES was indicted for stealing, on the 15th of September , 1 pair of stocks, value 18s.; 1 pair of dies, value 5s., and 3 taps, value 7s. , the goods of Charles Gray . THOMAS CARR . I am a smith and engineer, in the service of Mr. Charles Gray , in New Park-street, Southwark . On the 15th of September, 1831, the prisoner came to his shop to me, and said he came from Mr. Embleton, to borrow a pair of stocks and dies, as he had a job to do for Mr. Magnay; I knew Mr. Embleton to be
_source.title: JAMES JEFFERIES. Theft; simple larceny (from 1827). 6th September 1832.

text: borrow these articles. JOHN MILTON . I produce the stocks and dies, which were pawned with me on the 17th of September, 1831. JOHN JARVIS . (<mark>Police</mark>-constable C 13). I took the prisoner on another charge. Prisoner's Defence. I only borrowed them for work. GUILTY . - Aged 28. Transported for Seven Years .

_source.text: 1825. GEORGE SHAW was indicted for stealing, on the 23rd of March , 20 sovereigns, 1 half-sovereign, and three 5l. bank notes, the property of Samuel Farrington , from his person . SAMUEL FARRINGTON, I am a canal boatman , and live in Staffordshire. On the 23rd of March I was in London' and met a person who asked me to go and drink with him at the New London-bridge tap ; I went with him - he was a farmer, who said he had been on foot ever since ten o'clock, that he was fatigued, and was going to
_source.title: GEORGE SHAW. Theft; pocketpicking. 6th September 1832.

text: ; I was there an hour - the other man did not touch my money at all, I believe: I kept my eye on the prisoner, but he deceived me, or some what else did - I felt the same bulk in my pokcet, as I went along; I am not mistaken in the prisoner. JOHN BARNES (<mark>Police</mark>-constable H 168.) I was in East

_source.text: Before Mr. Justice Patteson. 1827. JOSEF RAMON DE SUSTACHA was indicted for that he feloniously did assault William Palmer , and feloniously did strike, cut, and wound him in and upon the back part of his head, with intent to disable him . 2nd COUNT, with intent to do him some grievous bodily harm. _source.title: JOSEF RAMON DE SUSTACHA. Breaking Peace; wounding. 6th September 1832.

text: action or geature: my head was about three feet from the lashing - he made the second blow at my head; it could not be made at the lashing - I was below him, and stooped with my head downwards to get it from the blow; I received the blow on the back part of the top of my head; the <mark>surgeon</mark> ordered me

lighter. ROBERT BOWIE . I am a <mark>surgeon</mark>. _source.text: Before Mr. Baron Bailey. 1828. MARY McCARTHY was indicted for feloniously killing and slaying Margaret Sheehy . SARAH BURLEY . I live in Great St. Andrew-street, Seven-dials ; Margaret Sheehy lived right opposite me- the prisoner is her sister; they did not live together. On the 21st of August, after twelve o'clock at night, I heard the deceased call Murder! and then the prisoner ran out of the gateway of the house which the deceased lived in; the deceased threw a handful of mud into the prisone
_source.title: MARY McCARTHY. Killing; manslaughter. 6th September 1832.

discover her voice among the persons quarrelling, till I heard her out in the street. ANN EVANS . I live at No. 16, Great St. Andrew-street- Sheehy lived at No. 15; there is a gateway between her house and mine. _source.text: NEW COURT. SATURDAY, SEPTEMBER 8. Fourth Middlesex Jury, before Mr. Common Sergeant. 1837. ANN JEFFRIES was indicted for stealing, on the 18th of July , 13 yards of printed cotton, value 3s. 3d. , the goods of William Sharman . WILLIAM SHARMAN . I live in Chiswell-street , and am a draper . On the 18th of July the prisoner walked about six feet into my shop, and took a piece of print; she ran out - I and my assistant followed her; she partly dropped the print on the pavement, but held one end of
_source.title: ANN JEFFRIES. Theft; simple larceny (from 1827). 6th September 1832.

text: . How near were you to her? A. About three yards; I am sure she dropped it. HENRY BEAN (<mark>Police</mark>-constable G 111). I took the prisoner and have the print. GUILTY . Aged 16. - Confined One Month .
